english.title: Carrier - fail ensure quantity carried not exceeded / placard displayed

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2007

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being the carrier of goods or equipment subject to the Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2007, namely **(..SPECIFY THE CHARACTER OF THE GOODS / EQUIPMENT..), which were in a vehicle namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..), at **(..SPECIFY LOCATION..) in

(A)_[a container,]_
(B)_[a multiple-element gas container,]_
(C)_[an uncertified multiple-element gas container,]_
(D)_[a tank-container,]_
(E)_[a portable tank,]_
(F)_[a demountable tank,]_

failed to ensure that

(G)_[the quantities being carried did not exceed the total threshold for those goods' transport category]_
(H)_[the vehicle displayed orange placards in accordance with regulation 53(4)]_
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 53(4), and 91 of and Schedule 7 to the Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2007 and section 33(1)(c) and (3) of the Health and Safety at Work etc Act 1974.

english.notes:
Important: these Regulations have been replaced by the Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2009.
(i) For further guidance see the prosecution guide.
(ii) In the first instance a prohibition notice under section 22 of the Health and Safety at Work Act 1974 should be considered subject to current HSE policy. Failure to comply with that prohibition should result in prosecution. Care should however be taken to obtain evidence to prove that the operator in the interim period had not complied with and therefore discharged the prohibition notice.
(iii) Where there is evidence of multiple offences, blatant disregard of the regulations or there has been previous advice, prosecution should also be considered.
(iv) The information specified in ADR 5.4 and 5.5 where relevant should form part of the transportation documents.
(v) The word "appropriate is open to interpretation
(vi) A prohibition notice is appropriate if the information is so lacking that the inspector is unable to identify what is being carried

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: A fine.

None
